chunks: And I implore you by Allah,
that you should not be that Imam of this nation who will be killed,
for it has been said: An Imam of this nation will be killed, after which killing and fighting will be made open for them until the Day of Judgment,
and he will confuse their affairs and spread trials in them,
so they will not discern the truth from falsehood, they will surge in it like waves, and be tossed about in it.
So do not become a carrying beast for Marwan, so that he may drag you wherever he wishes, despite your seniority of age and length of life.
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Hasan (AS) refuse to be the Imam under Marwan ibn al-Hakam?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns Hasan ibn Ali against accepting the caliphate under Marwan ibn al-Hakam, predicting that it would lead to a prolonged era of civil strife (*fitan*) and confusion until the Day of Judgment. He cautions that Hasan would become a mere instrument (*sayyiqah*) for Marwan, losing his independent authority and becoming a source of division rather than guidance. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of the Umayyad period as a time where political legitimacy was compromised by dynastic ambition, leading to the 'boiling' of the community in turmoil.
